android.note: Most often "Android" means the phone system: "My phone runs on Android."

hook.note: Most often "hook" means a curved piece for hanging things: "Hang your coat on the hook."

hehe.note: Informal; used in texts and chats to show quiet laughing.
ex: She texted me "hehe" after my silly joke.
Hehe, I took the last piece of pizza.
He always ends his funny messages with "hehe."
Why do you write "hehe" in every message?

fa.note: Also spelled "fah." In capitals, "FA" often means Football Association: "the FA Cup."
ex: In the scale, fa comes right after mi.
The singer held the fa note for a long time.
Our music teacher asked us to sing fa again.
Can you play fa on the piano for me?

snowboarding.note: Uncountable. We say "go snowboarding": "Let's go snowboarding this weekend."
ex: We go snowboarding in the mountains every winter.
Snowboarding is harder than it looks at first.
Is there a good place for snowboarding near here?
My brother hurt his knee while he was snowboarding.
Doctors once used chloroform to put patients to sleep.
Chloroform is a clear liquid with a sweet smell.
In old movies, criminals often put chloroform on a cloth.
Our chemistry lab keeps chloroform in a locked cabinet.

accelerator.note: In everyday American English, people say "gas pedal."
ex: Press the accelerator gently when the light turns green.
He put his foot down hard on the accelerator.
The accelerator is the pedal on the right.
The car moved forward when she pressed the accelerator.
She works for a biotech company near the university.
Biotech is growing fast in our city.
Many young scientists want a job in biotech.
The biotech firm made a new vaccine against flu.

filament.note: Also the thin wire inside a light bulb: "The bulb's filament broke."
ex: My 3D printer uses a roll of plastic filament.
Which color of filament do you need for this model?
Store the filament in a dry box after printing.
Under the microscope, you can see thin filaments inside the cell.

adhesive.note: In everyday speech, people usually say "glue."

hummus.note: Uncountable: some hummus, a lot of hummus (not "a hummus").
ex: I like to eat hummus with fresh carrots.
This hummus is very creamy and a little spicy.
Can you buy some hummus at the store today?
We had hummus and warm bread for lunch.

fleece.note: Also a sheep's wool. "A fleece" is often a warm jacket made of this fabric.
ex: I wear a fleece when it's cold outside.
This fleece is warm, light, and easy to wash.
He zipped up his blue fleece before the hike.
Do you have this fleece in a bigger size?

biceps.note: "Biceps" is singular and plural: "one biceps, two biceps."

ex: The letter B is a consonant, and A is a vowel.
Some English consonants are hard for learners to say.
How many consonants are there in the word "street"?
This word starts with two consonants together.
We played snooker at the pub after work.
He watches snooker on TV every weekend.
Snooker is very popular in Britain.
Can you teach me how to play snooker?

resonance.note: Also an emotional effect: "The story has resonance for many people."

hydra.note: Also the many-headed monster in Greek myths.

compost.note: Uncountable: some compost, a lot of compost (not "a compost").

liqueur.note: Do not confuse with "liquor," which means any strong alcohol.

gelatin.note: Uncountable: "some gelatin" or "a packet of gelatin."

puma.note: In the US, this animal is more often called a "cougar" or "mountain lion."
ex: A puma was seen near the hiking trail.
The puma hunts deer high in the mountains.
In America, pumas are also called cougars or mountain lions.
Our zoo has a young puma and two bears.
Some animals practice cannibalism when there is little food.
The movie is about cannibalism on a lonely island.
Cannibalism happens in some spiders and fish.
Scientists study cannibalism in insects and other animals.

congresswoman.note: A woman in the US Congress. Plural: congresswomen.
ex: The congresswoman visited our school last week.
I wrote a letter to my congresswoman about the park.
The congresswoman voted for the new law.
She was elected congresswoman two years ago.

ivory.note: Most often "ivory" means the hard white material of elephant tusks: "Selling ivory is illegal."

ex: In history class, we learned about the proletariat.
The proletariat is another name for the working class.
The party said it spoke for the proletariat.
The book describes the hard life of the proletariat.
He wore an old tweed jacket to the meeting.
Tweed is a warm, strong cloth made of wool.
Her winter skirt is made of gray tweed.
Do you have this coat in brown tweed?

barter.note: Uncountable. Also a verb: "They barter food for tools."

bushel.note: A unit for measuring grain and fruit, used mainly in the US.

ex: We watched the geyser shoot hot water into the air.
This geyser erupts about once every hour.
Iceland has many famous hot geysers.
Please don't stand too close to the geyser.

barman.note: British. In the US, people usually say "bartender." Plural: barmen.
ex: The barman poured us two glasses of beer.
Can you ask the barman for the menu?
He works as a barman at a small hotel.
The friendly barman knows the names of all his guests.
